The calibration process hinges on comparing an evidence sample against a database. The initial sample was not validated against the actual database, introducing a systemic bias. Excluding PENDING, VOID, and PUSH outcomes corrects for this bias, revealing that the sample underestimated model performance. The structural absence of CLV data in the database implies that any CLV-based metrics are fundamentally flawed. This leads to a reevaluation of confidence intervals and model skill assessments. The bias direction is conservative, meaning the model appears less skilled than it actually is. The implications extend beyond calibration into operational integrity of GSE’s predictive models.
